title: Clinical Efficacy of a Gardenia Blue and Fluoride-Containing Plaque Disclosing Agent: A Randomized Controlled Trial
content: Dental plaque is a primary etiological factor in common oral diseases such as dental caries and periodontal disease. Accurate visualization and effective removal of plaque are essential for maintaining oral health. However, conventional tar-based dye plaque disclosing agents have raised concerns due to potential cytotoxicity and difficulty in stain removal, prompting the need for safer, natural alternatives. This randomized, single-blind, crossover clinical trial aimed to evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of a novel natural dye-based plaque disclosing agent derived from Gardenia blue, compared to a conventional tar-based disclosing agent. A total of 100 healthy adults (aged 20–45 years) participated in the study. Each participant sequentially used both disclosing agents in a randomized order. Plaque staining effectiveness was assessed using the Patient Hygiene Performance (PHP) index and standardized intraoral photography. Stain retention was evaluated after 10 minutes, and ease of removal was assessed after water rinsing and toothbrushing. Adverse reactions were monitored throughout the study. Both disclosing agents demonstrated strong spatial concordance in plaque staining (Pearson r = 0.75–0.97, p < 0.001). The natural dye-based agent showed comparable plaque visualization effectiveness to the tar-based agent and significantly superior ease of removal (Cohen’s d = 0.78–1.40, p < 0.001). No adverse effects or mucosal irritation were reported with the natural dye-based agent. The Gardenia blue-based natural dye disclosing agent is a clinically effective and safe alternative to conventional tar-based products for plaque visualization and oral hygiene education.
